archetype.name: Lost Season
archetype.definition: A team coming off 50 wins and 15 playoff wins collapsed to 19-63. Its offense fell from the league's top third to near the bottom, and its usual defensive and rebounding problems had nothing left to cover for them.

report.headline: From 15 playoff wins to 19-63: the offense that carried Indiana disappeared

recap.finish: 19-63, last in the Central; missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a bad team, not an unlucky one. Indiana finished with a Net Rtg of -7.9 (26th), an offense ranked 29th by ORtg at 110.9 and a defense ranked 23rd at 118.8. Both ends ran well below the league, by 4.9 points per 100 possessions on offense and 3.1 on defense. Last year's 50-32 team had a 116.5 ORtg and ranked ninth on offense. In 2023-24 the offense sat second at 121. The shooting that drove those teams slipped to a 56.8 TS % (24th) from 59.4. With the offense gone, there was nothing to hide a defense that has graded poorly in most of these recent seasons.

The record never gave anyone a reason to believe. Indiana opened 0-5 in October, went 4-11 in November and 2-12 in December, and stood 6-28 by New Year's. January was the one competitive month, 7-8, with the fewest points allowed per game of any month at 116.8. Then the bottom fell out. February (2-9) and March (2-13) were the worst defensive months of the year, at 124.09 and 125.2 points allowed a game. A 16-game losing streak was the year's signature, and the team never won more than three straight.

The roster explains a lot. Pascal Siakam was the one player who drove winning. He made the All-Star team, scored 1,485 points on a 30.1 USG %, ranked 16th of 93 on his tab, and carried a +5.5 On-Off. T.J. McConnell (21st of 89 at PG, BPM 2.5) was the best guard by the numbers. The efficient bigs did their part: Jay Huff played all 82 games at a 59.8 TS % with 119 threes, and Ivica Zubac posted a team-high 4.2 Win Shares in only 48 games. The heavy-minute pieces around them dragged. Andrew Nembhard led the backcourt in minutes with a -4.1 On-Off. Jarace Walker played 76 games at a -5.8 On-Off and 0.5 Win Shares. Aaron Nesmith was limited to 45 games with a -3.4 BPM. The listed wings combined for only 1,701 minutes. Every group graded poorly: backcourt D-, wings D, frontcourt D+.

The structural weaknesses were on the glass and in forcing mistakes. Indiana ranked 29th in ORB % (21.7) and 29th in REB % (47.3), and it was near the bottom in rebounds allowed to point guards and power forwards. The defense did hold opponents' threes down, with Opp 3P % 12th and threes allowed to shooting guards and small forwards near the league's fewest. But opponents' overall Opp eFG % was 24th, and the defense forced turnovers at a rate of only 22nd. Teams scored inside and kept their possessions.

The ending was slightly better than the whole. The last 10 games went 3-7 with a -1.6 point differential per game, 6.39 points better than the season. Scoring rose by 5.67 points a game, and two of the losses came by a point against the Clippers and by seven against the Lakers. The final five, though, went 1-4, closing with losses to Philadelphia and Detroit. The W vs Pt Diff of -4 says the margin was worth about 23 wins. That is a little better than 19, but still one of the league's worst teams.

highlights.title: Siakam carried an All-Star load
highlights.body: Siakam was the engine of what little worked. He used 30.1% of possessions while on the floor, led the team in scoring, and Indiana was 5.5 points per 100 better with him on. He ranked 16th of 93 on his tab, and his production shows no sign of decline. The issue was the lack of help around him.

highlights.title: Efficient bigs: Huff and Zubac
highlights.body: The center spot was the roster's most productive. Huff answered the bell all 82 games, shooting a 59.8 TS % with 119 threes. Zubac produced a team-high 4.2 Win Shares in 48 games on a 62.2 TS % with 509 rebounds. They are the best reason the frontcourt graded highest of the three groups, even if a D+ is nothing to celebrate.

highlights.title: Perimeter three-point defense held
highlights.body: Opponents shot 35.5% from three, 12th in the league and a bit under the league average. Shooting guards and small forwards made fewer threes against Indiana than almost anywhere else. It is the one defensive habit worth building on.

lowlights.title: The offense fell off a cliff
lowlights.body: An offense that ranked ninth last year and second the year before finished 29th, with ORtg dropping to 110.9 from 116.5. Shooting efficiency fell across the board, and the team got to the line less than average. That makes this the season's defining collapse rather than a fluke stretch: it was below the league in every month.

lowlights.title: Losing the glass at both ends
lowlights.body: Indiana ranked 29th in ORB % and 29th in REB %, and opponents' power forwards and point guards out-rebounded their norms against it. Weak offensive rebounding is a long-running trait here, with similar rates in 2020-21 and last season. Without elite shooting, though, it cost far more.

lowlights.title: Rotation minutes with negative impact
lowlights.body: Walker and Nembhard played heavy minutes with On-Off marks of -5.8 and -4.1, and Walker produced 0.5 Win Shares across 76 games. The wings group was thin, with Nesmith missing time, and graded a D. The backcourt's D- was the worst of the three grades.

arc.note: A 6-28 start bottomed out further after a respectable 7-8 January. The defense then gave up 124-plus a game in February and March during a 16-game skid, before a slightly more competitive finish.

recap.nextYear: The pieces that worked are clear. Siakam was a genuine All-Star-level engine, McConnell was the best guard by the rankings, and Huff and Zubac gave efficient play at center. Everything else needs work. The backcourt (D-) and wings (D) graded near the bottom, and the wing minutes were thin. Rebounding at both ends was among the league's worst, and the defense forced too few turnovers. Luck explains only a sliver: the W vs Pt Diff of -4 means the margin looked like a 23-win team, not a hidden contender. The late-season scoring bump (+5.67 points a game over the last 10) is a small sample. The real question the numbers raise is whether the offense that ranked second and ninth the previous two years can return, because this year's defense was in line with what Indiana has usually been.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season with consistent results across months; a few key players missed significant time.
